issues.body:
This diff exists because the documented enum silently fell behind scripts/policy-resolve.py:55 — 'registry-selftest' was added to GATE_PROFILES and put into shipped use by the registry's own row (policy/repos.toml:197) without the field-reference comment being updated. Nothing in the self-test suite compares the two, so the same drift can recur in either direction the next time a profile is added or retired, and a future reader following this comment block could believe a valid profile is unsupported (or, worse in the other direction, that a retired one is still valid).

This is genuinely a nit and NOT a condition of approval: the comment is prose, the validator is the real authority and is unchanged, and demanding a new test harness as the price of a one-line docs correction would be scope creep on an otherwise clean fix. Recording it only so the underlying cause is visible rather than fixed-and-forgotten.
issues.fix_hint: Optional, and reasonably deferred to a separate change: add a small non-vacuous assertion to the policy-resolve.py --self-test that parses the `#   gate_profile           = ...` line out of policy/repos.toml, extracts the double-quoted tokens, and asserts the resulting set equals GATE_PROFILES exactly (set equality, not a subset check — a subset check would pass vacuously if the comment listed nothing). To keep it non-vacuous, pair it with a negative case proving the comparison flips red when the two differ, in the same style as the existing staged-row guard at policy-resolve.py:1043-1054. If the comment's format is considered too brittle to parse, the honest alternative is to leave it as-is rather than ship a check that silently no-ops when the regex stops matching.
issues.title: No guard prevents this comment from drifting out of sync with GATE_PROFILES again

verdict.summary:
Single-line documentation fix to the field-reference comment block in policy/repos.toml: the documented gate_profile enum now includes "registry-selftest". This corrects genuine doc-vs-code drift and is COMPLETE and ACCURATE.

Verified against the enforcement points (none of which this diff touches):

1. Authority match. scripts/policy-resolve.py:55 defines GATE_PROFILES = {"none", "lint-only", "crate-scoped", "workspace", "registry-selftest"}, and _policy_row (line 255-256) rejects anything outside it with "unknown gate_profile". The updated comment is now an EXACT set match with the validator — no member added that the validator would reject, none omitted.

2. The profile is real, not aspirational. worker-live.sh run_gate has a live `registry-selftest)` branch (line 874) implementing the python --self-test suite + bash -n/actionlint, and it is demonstrably fail-closed: no runnable suite dies (line 2072), an unvalidated touched control file dies (2073-2074), an empty changed-path list dies (1960), and an unavailable dependency is ENV-BLOCKED rather than treated as a pass (1954). So the docs are not advertising a profile with no worker branch.

3. Already in shipped use. The registry's own row (policy/repos.toml:197) has carried gate_profile = "registry-selftest" for some time; the comment block was simply stale. This diff makes documentation catch up to reality — it does not enable, widen, or introduce anything.

4. Completeness. The enum is enumerated in exactly two places repo-wide (the repos.toml comment and GATE_PROFILES). Greps over *.md and the whole tree surface no other stale listing, so there is no half-updated second copy.

Trust-plane lens: zero behavioural surface. No validator, route, self-test, arm path, permissions block or match_labels set is deleted, relaxed or skipped; no default-allow path is opened.
